title: Bell pepper Nutrient Deficiency: Signs, Causes and the Fertilizer That Fixes It
metaTitle: Bell pepper Nutrient Deficiency: Signs and Fertilizer Fix
metaDescription: Bell pepper nutrient deficiency shows in the leaves. See the signs of nitrogen, calcium and potassium in atsal, how to be sure, and the fertilizer to apply.
excerpt: Bell pepper nutrient deficiency is one of the first things to check when the leaves of your atsal (bell pepper) turn yellow, purple or burnt at the edges. On Philippine farms the usual ones are nitrogen, calcium, potassium, phosphorus, magnesium, sulfur, zinc, iron and manganese. This guide shows where each one starts, how to be sure, and the fertilizer that fixes it.

heroImage.alt: Pile of green bell peppers with tan, papery sunken patches at the blossom end from calcium shortage
heroImage.credit: Edward Sikora, Auburn University, Bugwood.org, CC BY 3.0 US, via ipmimages.org

blocks.text: Start with one question: did the change begin on the old leaves or on the young ones? Nitrogen, potassium, phosphorus and magnesium move inside the plant, so a shortage shows on the old, lower leaves first. But calcium, sulfur, zinc, iron and manganese stay where the plant first put them, so the young leaves and the growing tip show it first. After that, the color and the pattern narrow down which bell pepper nutrient deficiency you have, and a soil test confirms it. Each one below has its signs, its causes and its fix.

blocks.text: Before you buy fertilizer for a bell pepper nutrient deficiency

So use the table to pick the likeliest bell pepper nutrient deficiency, then read its section below. Also keep in mind that dry soil, standing water, cold nights, a pest or a disease can look the same. That is why it pays to check the roots and the whole field first.
Nitrogen deficiency in bell pepper

Growth is badly held back. Lower leaves turn yellow and die early, and the rest of the leaves stay small and pale yellow green. Fewer fruits set and fruit size drops. You see it most at this stage: from transplanting through fruiting.
Why nitrogen deficiency happens in atsal
Sandy or light soils, heavy rain or irrigation, low organic matter, and raw straw or manure that ties up nitrogen.
How to tell it apart

Sulfur shortage starts on the youngest leaves at the top. Magnesium shortage keeps the main veins green on older leaves. To be sure, bottom leaves yellow first. Confirm with a soil test and leaf tissue test.
What to apply for nitrogen deficiency

Side dress urea or ammonium sulfate based on the soil test, in split doses. For a quick green up, KAU gives a urea spray at 10 grams per liter of water every 15 days for chilli, which is the same species.

Sold here with nitrogen: **Atlas Granular Urea** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (46 0 0), **YaraVera Viking Ship Granular Urea** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (46 0 0), **Planters Products Granular Urea** by Planters Products, Inc. (46 0 0) and **Harbest Granular Urea** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (46 0 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [urea fertilizer](/blog/urea-fertilizer), and the page on [nitrogen deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/nitrogen-deficiency) in every crop. In anee.io, Anee, the [smart farm technician](/features/ai-agricultural-technician), reads a photo of the leaf and tells you which nutrient is short.
To keep it away, add compost to the beds and split nitrogen through the season.
Calcium deficiency in bell pepper

blocks.alt: Pile of green bell peppers with tan, papery sunken patches at the blossom end from calcium shortage
blocks.caption: Photo: Edward Sikora, Auburn University, Bugwood.org, CC BY 3.0 US, via ipmimages.org

blocks.text: Large sunken, water soaked spots form near the blossom end of the fruit. They start soft, then dry, harden and turn black, and mould may grow on them. Several spots can form on one fruit, and on young fruit the whole end may rot and the fruit drop. Upper leaves may yellow between the veins with dark brown dead spots on the edges of the youngest leaves. You see it most at this stage: early fruit growth. It can appear suddenly and spread over a field in hot dry weather.
Why calcium deficiency happens in atsal
Too little calcium reaching the fruit, usually because of uneven watering or dry soil. Acid sandy soils, salty soil, high nitrogen or potassium, and large fruits raise the risk.
How to tell it apart

Sunscald makes pale, papery patches on the side facing the sun. Bacterial soft rot is wet and smelly from the start. To be sure, spots at the blossom end of young fruit after dry spells. Then a soil test for calcium and pH.
What to apply for calcium deficiency

Keep the soil evenly moist and mulch. On acid soil, KAU suggests lime at about 250 kg per hectare when pH is 5.5 to 6, or about 840 kg per hectare in two doses when pH is 3.5 to 4.5. Gypsum on soil that is not acid. Remove damaged fruits.

Sold here with calcium: **Planters Products Lifelime** by Planters Products, Inc. (50.59 percent CaO), **Macrock Limestone** by Donumdei 1 Corp. (36 to 42 percent calcium), **Calcic Lime** by Mindanao Agriplus Corporation (35.52 percent calcium) and **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource Limited Corporation (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [fertilizer for tomatoes](/blog/fertilizer-for-tomatoes), and the page on [calcium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/calcium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, lime acid soil before planting, water on a steady schedule, use calcium nitrate as part of the nitrogen, and avoid heavy ammonium fertilizer.
Potassium deficiency in bell pepper

Plants are short with small leaves that bend down and look limp and wilted while staying dark green. Leaf edges and the areas between veins yellow, and small sunken, sometimes whitish spots form on the edges. On older leaves these turn into dead patches that join until the leaf looks scorched. You see it most at this stage: fruiting.
Why potassium deficiency happens in atsal
Sandy or acid soils, heavy rain or irrigation that leaches potassium, drought, and soils high in magnesium.
How to tell it apart

Wilting from root disease or dry soil comes without the spotting and edge burn. Magnesium shortage yellows between the veins without wilting. To be sure, soil test for potassium and a leaf tissue test.
What to apply for potassium deficiency

Apply muriate of potash or sulfate of potash based on the soil test, in split doses. For immediate relief, KAU gives a morning spray of sulfate of potash at 10 grams per liter of water with a sticker for chilli, the same species.

Sold here with potassium: **Atlas Muriate of Potash** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Philphos Muriate of Potash** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Harbest Granular Muriate of Potash** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (0 0 60) and **Swire Muriate of Potash** by Swire Agrotech Agricultural Products Inc. (0 0 60). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [potash fertilizer](/blog/potash-fertilizer), and the page on [potassium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/potassium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, include potash at planting and in side dressings during fruiting.
Phosphorus deficiency in bell pepper

In severe cases the whole plant and its leaves are much smaller and the older leaves wilt. Leaves look mottled yellow with dark green patches. A narrow dead strip can form along the main vein near the leaf base. Larger yellow spots near the edge turn grey and die. Fruits are shorter and narrower than normal. You see it most at this stage: seedling and early growth, and in cool or wet spells.
Why phosphorus deficiency happens in atsal
Acid or very alkaline soils, iron rich soils that hold phosphorus, low organic matter, cold or wet soils and poor roots.
How to tell it apart
Root rot also causes wilting and small plants. Check the roots for rot. To be sure, soil test for available phosphorus and pH.
What to apply for phosphorus deficiency

Apply phosphorus near the roots based on the soil test. KAU lists single superphosphate for a quick fix and rock phosphate or bone meal for the long term. Notes phosphorus is best taken up near pH 6.2 to 7.0.

Sold here with phosphorus: **Triple Super Phosphate** by Newman Chemicals Corporation (0 46 0), **Sagrex Duofos Granular Guano Phosphate** by Sagrex Corporation (0 22 0 (guano phosphate)), **Philphos 18 46 0** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0 (diammonium phosphate)) and **Atlas Di Ammonium Phosphate** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [16 20 0 fertilizer](/blog/16-20-0-fertilizer), and the page on [phosphorus deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/phosphorus-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, use a phosphorus starter at transplanting and add compost.
Magnesium deficiency in bell pepper

Older leaves turn pale between the veins while the main veins and a band along them stay green. Sometimes it begins as a faint yellowing at the leaf edge that moves toward the centre. In advanced cases dead patches start at the edge and spread inward, and growth and yield drop. You see it most at this stage: fruit set and fruit filling.
Why magnesium deficiency happens in atsal
Sandy or acid soils, soils rich in potassium, heavy potash fertilizer, and cold wet periods.
How to tell it apart
Manganese and iron shortage start on young leaves, where even the smallest veins stay green. To be sure, soil test for magnesium and potassium, and a leaf tissue test.
What to apply for magnesium deficiency

KAU gives magnesium sulfate in a band near the plants at about 80 kg per hectare (32 kg per acre) for chilli, the same species. A foliar spray of magnesium sulfate gives faster relief. Do not apply magnesium and potassium fertilizer together.

Sold here with magnesium: **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource Limited Corporation (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium), **YaraTera KRISTA MgS** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (16 percent MgO and 13 percent sulfur), **Magnepro** by Ramgo International Corporation (16 percent MgO and 12.8 percent sulfur) and **Lucky Planters Magnesium Sulphate Heptahydrate (Epsom Salt)** by Mindanao Agriplus Corporation (16.27 percent MgO and 13 percent sulfur). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [complete fertilizer](/blog/complete-fertilizer-14-14-14), and the page on [magnesium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/magnesium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, use dolomite on acid soil and keep potash in line with the soil test.
Sulfur deficiency in bell pepper

The youngest leaves at the top turn an even light green while the veins stay darker. Held against light, the green veins show. Some young leaves get a yellow green color between the veins that starts at the leaf base. Plants are stunted with short spaces between leaves. You see it most at this stage: early growth on light soils.
Why sulfur deficiency happens in atsal
Acid, sandy, low organic matter soils, waterlogged soils, and fertilizer programs with no sulfur.
How to tell it apart
Nitrogen shortage starts on the old lower leaves. Iron shortage gives a sharper yellow with very green veins on young leaves. To be sure, soil test for sulfate and a leaf tissue test.
What to apply for sulfur deficiency

Use ammonium sulfate or sulfate of potash in the next side dressing. KAU gives sulfur dust at about 25 kg per hectare (10 kg per acre) on sulfur deficient soil for chilli, and gypsum on alkaline soil.

Sold here with sulfur: **Farmfix Sulfur** by Philippine FarmFix, Inc. (99 percent sulfur), **VSI Sulfur Powder** by Newman Chemicals Corporation (99.5 percent sulfur), **Atlas Ammosul** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (21 0 0 with 24 percent sulfur) and **Philphos 21 0 0** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (21 0 0 (ammonium sulfate)). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [ammonium sulfate fertilizer](/blog/ammonium-sulfate-21-0-0), and the page on [sulfur deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/sulfur-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, include some sulfur fertilizer every season.
Zinc deficiency in bell pepper
Plants are stunted with shortened spaces between leaves, and the leaves are smaller than normal. Young leaves may also yellow between the veins. You see it most at this stage: vegetative growth.
Why zinc deficiency happens in atsal
High pH soils, soils rich in phosphorus or given heavy phosphorus, organic soils, and cold wet spells.
How to tell it apart

Virus diseases also stunt plants and shrink leaves. They usually come with mosaic or curling and insects such as aphids, thrips or whiteflies. To be sure, soil test for zinc and pH, and a leaf tissue test.
What to apply for zinc deficiency

KAU gives zinc sulfate in the soil at about 20 kg per hectare (8 kg per acre) for chilli. In severe cases a morning spray of zinc sulfate at 2 grams plus calcium carbonate at 2.5 grams per liter of water. Do not apply zinc together with phosphate fertilizer.

Sold here with zinc: **Harvester Zinc Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Universal Harvester, Inc. (22 percent zinc), **Great Planters Zinc Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Agway Chemicals Corp. (21 percent zinc), **Zinc Sulphate Monohydrate** by Petbowe Trading Corporation (33 percent zinc) and **YaraVita ZINTRAC 700** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (40 percent zinc). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [fertilizer with zinc](/blog/micronutrients-for-rice), and the page on [zinc deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/zinc-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, avoid phosphorus beyond the soil test and keep pH between 5 and 7.5.
Iron deficiency in bell pepper

The newest leaves at the shoot tips turn yellow green between the veins while the veins stay dark green at first. If the shortage lasts, the veins also pale and the whole leaf turns light. Plants can be shorter with limp leaves. You see it most at this stage: any stage, often after heavy watering or liming.
Why iron deficiency happens in atsal
High pH, calcareous or overlimed soils, waterlogged soils, and soils high in copper, manganese or zinc. On acid Philippine soils true iron shortage is uncommon, so check the pH and drainage first.
How to tell it apart
Magnesium shortage starts on old leaves. Manganese shortage also hits young leaves but leaves more small veins green. To be sure, soil pH test, then a soil or leaf test for iron.
What to apply for iron deficiency

Improve drainage and stop liming. KAU gives ferrous sulfate in the soil at about 15 kg per hectare (6 kg per acre) for chilli where a test confirms low iron. A foliar spray of ferrous sulfate or iron chelate greens leaves faster.

Sold here with iron: **Ferrous Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Cleveland Industries Inc. (20 percent iron), **Ferrous Sulfate Monohydrate** by Zetryl.Chem Phils., Inc. (30 percent iron), **Grow More Liquid Chelate Iron with Sulfur** by Sagrex Corporation (5 percent iron and 3 percent sulfur) and **Biozome** by Manchem Industries, Inc. (12 percent S, 12 percent Zn, 3 percent Mn, 1 percent Mg, 1 percent Fe, 1 percent Cu, 0.5 percent B, 0.05 percent Mo). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [iron deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/iron-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, do not overlime and keep beds well drained.
Manganese deficiency in bell pepper

Young leaves turn pale between the veins while the small veins stay dark green, giving a fine net pattern. Small dark dead spots can form in the pale areas. You see it most at this stage: vegetative growth and fruiting.
Why manganese deficiency happens in atsal
Organic or sandy soils, high pH, loose fluffy soils, and cold wet weather.
How to tell it apart
Iron shortage looks similar on young leaves. Magnesium shortage starts on old leaves and leaves only the main veins green. To be sure, soil pH and a leaf tissue test.
What to apply for manganese deficiency
KAU gives a manganese sulfate spray at 2 grams per liter of water for chilli, after a soil test confirms the need.

Sold here with manganese: **Manganese Sulfate** by Zetryl.Chem Phils., Inc. (31 percent manganese), **Tierramino Mn** by Unilox Far East Resources Inc. (12 percent manganese and 7 percent N), **Multimate** by Agway Chemicals Corp. (1.8 percent Mn, 2.8 percent Zn, 4 percent N, 4.5 percent S (w/v)) and **Biozome** by Manchem Industries, Inc. (12 percent S, 12 percent Zn, 3 percent Mn, 1 percent Mg, 1 percent Fe, 1 percent Cu, 0.5 percent B, 0.05 percent Mo). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [manganese deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/manganese-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, do not overlime.

blocks.title: Let a soil test decide the rate
blocks.text: A soil test is the surest check for any bell pepper nutrient deficiency. Before you buy, ask your Municipal Agriculture Office where to send a soil sample. The DA regional soil laboratories and the Bureau of Soils and Water Management test soil, and the result says how much of each fertilizer your atsal needs. That saves money, because extra fertilizer is money lost.

blocks.text: Bell pepper nutrient deficiency questions

items.q: Why are my atsal leaves turning yellow?
items.a: The most common cause is nitrogen deficiency: lower leaves yellow and fall early, and the whole plant looks pale and small. If the young leaves turn yellow first instead, look at sulfur deficiency.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes nitrogen deficiency in bell pepper?
items.a: Side dress urea or ammonium sulfate based on the soil test, in split doses. For a quick green up, KAU gives a urea spray at 10 grams per liter of water every 15 days for chilli, which is the same species.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes calcium deficiency in bell pepper?
items.a: Keep the soil evenly moist and mulch. On acid soil, KAU suggests lime at about 250 kg per hectare when pH is 5.5 to 6, or about 840 kg per hectare in two doses when pH is 3.5 to 4.5.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes potassium deficiency in bell pepper?
items.a: Apply muriate of potash or sulfate of potash based on the soil test, in split doses. For immediate relief, KAU gives a morning spray of sulfate of potash at 10 grams per liter of water with a sticker for chilli, the same species.

items.q: How do I know which nutrient my atsal lacks?
items.a: First look at where the change began, on the old leaves or the young ones, then at the color and the pattern. Next, confirm the bell pepper nutrient deficiency with a soil test or a leaf test before you buy fertilizer.
